enzyme_name: flavonol 3-O-glucoside 3"-O-p-coumaroyltransferase (BAHD-type acyl-CoA acyltransferase; protein not identified)
organism_context: plant secondary metabolism (MetaCyc PWY-7168, flavonol acylglucoside biosynthesis I)
rationale: No characterised protein performing the 3"-O-coumaroylation of kaempferol 3-O-glucoside could be retrieved; the activity sits in the BAHD acyl-CoA acyltransferase class, whose members are single-domain transferases, but the specific enzyme is unidentified so functionality is left unknown.
direction_note: Acyl transfer from a CoA thioester to a sugar hydroxyl is strongly exergonic and physiologically unidirectional, so the biosynthetic (left-to-right) sense is right and ModelSEED's reverse assignment would make the entry a CoA-dependent de-esterification that no BAHD enzyme performs.

enzyme_name: glutaredoxin (thioltransferase)
organism_context: Escherichia coli (EcoCyc RXN0-6256 is the classical HED/HEDS glutaredoxin assay reaction)
rationale: Reduction of 2-hydroxyethyl disulfide by GSH is the standard glutaredoxin thiol-disulfide oxidoreductase assay, a single catalytic activity; E. coli has three glutaredoxins that all run it (Grx2's GST-like fold is a separate caveat, not relevant to this chemistry).
direction_note: GSSG, the oxidised half of the couple that makes GSH-driven disulfide reduction irreversible, is absent (ModelSEED status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2), so the stored direction has nothing anchoring it; GSH reduces HED, it is not regenerated from thioglycol.

enzyme_name: D-cysteine desulfhydrase (DcyD / YedO)
organism_context: Salmonella typhimurium / Escherichia coli; fold-type II PLP-dependent lyase
rationale: The chemistry shown (D-cysteine losing H2S to give dehydroalanine/2-aminoacrylate) is the alpha,beta-elimination half of D-cysteine desulfhydrase, a single-activity PLP lyase; the subsequent hydration to pyruvate + NH3 is spontaneous and is split off into a separate entry.
direction_note: The enzyme only eliminates; re-addition of H2S to dehydroalanine to rebuild D-cysteine is not an activity it has, so ModelSEED's reverse direction is not supported by the enzymology.

enzyme_name: cytochrome P450 (CYP2E1-type microsomal monooxygenase) acting as N-nitrosodimethylamine denitrosase
organism_context: rat/human liver microsomes
rationale: Microsomal P450 catalyses both demethylation and denitrosation of NDMA (identical Km values indicate the same enzyme); denitrosation fragments the alpha-nitrosamino radical to nitric oxide plus N-methylformaldimine, which hydrolyses to formaldehyde + methylamine. P450s are single-activity monooxygenases.
direction_note: O2 and NADPH, which make the P450 oxidation irreversible, have been dropped and only H2O remains, so the stored direction rests on nothing; the degradative sense (NDMA consumed, NO released) is the real one.

enzyme_name: GDP-L-colitose-dependent alpha-colitosyltransferase (not identified)
organism_context: bacterial O-antigen biosynthesis; colitose transferase genes occur in rfb clusters of Salmonella enterica and Yersinia pseudotuberculosis O:6/O:7
rationale: No characterised colitosyltransferase acting on lacto-N-biose could be found; colitose transferases are known only as predicted glycosyltransferase ORFs in O-antigen gene clusters, so the catalysing protein and its functionality are unknown.
direction_note: NDP-sugar glycosyl transfer with GDP release is unidirectional in vivo; note the ModelSEED MI flag here comes from a corrupted formula on cpd33032 (stored as C75H122NO20P2 for a trisaccharide) rather than from any missing species, so the written chemistry is sound.

enzyme_name: 4-amino-4-deoxychorismate synthase (aminodeoxychorismate synthase, ADCS)
organism_context: fused single polypeptide in plants (Arabidopsis thaliana plastid-targeted PabA-PabB) and some bacteria; two separate associating subunits in Escherichia coli
rationale: In Arabidopsis the p-aminobenzoate branch of folate synthesis is initiated by one bifunctional PabA-PabB fusion protein carrying both the glutamine amidotransferase and the ADC synthase activities; the E. coli counterpart is a two-polypeptide complex, which does not count as bifunctional.
direction_note: The product 4-amino-4-deoxychorismate is missing (status MI:C:-10/H:-9/N:-1/O:-5), leaving the nonsensical 'Gln + chorismate -> Glu'; the real reaction is pulled forward by glutamine hydrolysis and is a committed biosynthetic step.

enzyme_name: 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate oxidase (ACC oxidase / ethylene-forming enzyme)
organism_context: plants; also characterised in Agaricus bisporus
rationale: ACO is a single-activity Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dioxygenase-superfamily oxidase converting ACC to ethylene + HCN + CO2 with O2 and ascorbate; no second catalytic activity is reported on the chain.
direction_note: Dehydroascorbate (C6H6O6) is missing from the products (status MI:C:-6/H:-6/O:-6), but O2 consumption plus CO2 and HCN release already make the reaction irreversibly forward, so ModelSEED's reverse direction is wrong independently of the imbalance.

enzyme_name: hydroxymethylphosphonate dehydrogenase of the phosphinothricin (php) cluster (PhpE-type NAD(P)-dependent dehydrogenase)
organism_context: Streptomyces viridochromogenes DSM 40736 / S. hygroscopicus, phosphinothricin tripeptide (bialaphos) pathway
rationale: The step belongs to the PTT pathway, where an NAD(P)-dependent dehydrogenase of the php cluster oxidises hydroxymethylphosphonate to phosphonoformaldehyde, but the retrieved literature did not let me confirm the individual protein or test it for a second activity.
direction_note: The pathway consumes hydroxymethylphosphonate and produces the aldehyde, i.e. the oxidative left-to-right sense; the three H+ on the product side look like a proton-balancing artefact rather than real chemistry.

enzyme_name: acyl-glucose-dependent anthocyanin 7-O-glucosyltransferase (Dg AA7GT), a glycoside hydrolase family 1 protein
organism_context: Delphinium grandiflorum (homologue Dc AA5GT in Dianthus caryophyllus)
rationale: MetaCyc PWY-7256 is the delphinium acyl-glucose-dependent route in which the GH1 protein Dg AA7GT installs the 7-O-glucose on cyanidin 3-O-glucoside; the 'beta-glucosidase' label reflects its GH1 ancestry, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: The real glucosyl donor is an aromatic acyl-glucose (p-hydroxybenzoyl-glucose), abstracted here to free D-glucose + H2O; in vivo this enzyme ADDS the 7-O-glucose, which is the direction ModelSEED stores, whereas the LLM's hydrolytic sense destroys the product the pathway exists to make.

enzyme_name: ADP-ribosyl cyclase / NAD+ glycohydrolase (CD38; Aplysia ADP-ribosyl cyclase)
organism_context: mammalian CD38/BST-1 ectoenzymes; Aplysia californica soluble cyclase
rationale: CD38 and the Aplysia cyclase are a single polypeptide carrying cyclase, glycohydrolase and base-exchange activities and are routinely described as multifunctional; the same active-site chemistry acting on the 2'-phosphorylated nucleotide gives 2'-phospho-cADPR from NAADP.
direction_note: Cleaving the pyridinium N-glycoside of NAADP and cyclising onto adenine N1 with release of nicotinic acid is the favourable cyclase direction, exactly as for NAD+ -> cADPR + nicotinamide; the LLM's direction would require rebuilding a pyridinium nucleotide from free nicotinate.

enzyme_name: violaxanthin de-epoxidase (VDE / NPQ1)
organism_context: plants (Arabidopsis thaliana, spinach); lipocalin-family, thylakoid lumen
rationale: VDE is a single-activity lumenal lipocalin that de-epoxidises violaxanthin to antheraxanthin (then zeaxanthin) using ascorbate as reductant; the opposing epoxidation is run by a different protein, zeaxanthin epoxidase, with O2 + NADPH.
direction_note: Dehydroascorbate is missing (status MI:C:-6/H:-6/O:-6), so the equation reads as a freely reversible hydration; it is the ascorbate/DHA couple that fixes the de-epoxidation direction, and the reverse reaction belongs to a different enzyme entirely.

enzyme_name: CTP:CMP-3-deoxy-D-manno-octulosonate cytidylyltransferase (CMP-KDO synthetase, KdsB)
organism_context: Escherichia coli and other Gram-negative bacteria (LPS inner core)
rationale: KdsB is a single-activity nucleotidyltransferase of known primary structure with no second catalytic function reported on the polypeptide.
direction_note: The product CMP-KDO is absent from the equation (status MI:C:-17/H:-23/N:-3/O:-15/P:-1); the real reaction is pulled forward by pyrophosphate release and is the committed step supplying CMP-KDO for lipid A.

enzyme_name: limonoid UDP-glucosyltransferase (Citrus unshiu cuGT) - assignment disputed
organism_context: Citrus spp.; EC 2.4.1.210
rationale: The only cloned EC 2.4.1.210 candidate, Citrus cuGT, was re-tested and shown not to glucosylate limonoate A-ring lactone or limonoate at all (it is active on flavonoids), so the enzyme actually responsible for limonoid glucosylation is currently unidentified.
direction_note: The glucoside product is missing (status MI:C:-32/H:-42/O:-14) and a spurious H2O is present, but with UDP-glucose as the explicit donor the transfer direction (UDP-glucose consumed, UDP released) is unambiguous.

enzyme_name: flavonol 3-O-glucoside 6"-O-p-coumaroyltransferase (BAHD-type acyl-CoA acyltransferase; protein not identified)
organism_context: plant secondary metabolism (MetaCyc PWY-7168; product tribuloside = kaempferol 3-O-(6"-O-p-coumaroyl)-glucoside)
rationale: As for the 3"-isomer (rxn47118), no characterised protein for this 6"-O-coumaroylation could be retrieved; the class (BAHD acyl-CoA acyltransferase) is single-domain, but the catalysing enzyme is unidentified so functionality is left unknown.
direction_note: CoA-thioester to ester acyl transfer is exergonic and unidirectional, so the biosynthetic left-to-right sense is correct and ModelSEED's reverse direction is not an activity of acyl-CoA-dependent acyltransferases.

enzyme_name: apicidin-cluster polyketide/fatty-acid synthase plus a separate aminotransferase (no single enzyme)
organism_context: Fusarium semitectum / F. fujikuroi apicidin (APS/APF) gene clusters
rationale: Four rounds of decarboxylative chain extension plus a transamination are collapsed into one entry; in Fusarium these are carried out by an iterative polyketide/fatty-acid synthase of the apicidin cluster together with a separate aminotransferase, so no single protein catalyses the reaction as written.
direction_note: Decarboxylative Claisen chain extension from acetyl-CoA + malonyl-CoA is irreversible, so the biosynthetic sense is correct even though the entry is grossly unbalanced (NADPH, CO2, CoA and the amino donor all absent; status MI:C:-109/H:-140/N:-34/...).

enzyme_name: anhydrotetracycline C4 N,N-dimethyltransferase (OxyT)
organism_context: Streptomyces rimosus oxytetracycline cluster (minimal ATC-forming enzyme set)
rationale: OxyT is the SAM-dependent C4-amine methyltransferase required for anhydrotetracycline formation; running the same methylation twice (mono- then di-methyl) is one catalytic activity, not two.
direction_note: SAM-dependent N-methylation with SAH release is effectively irreversible, so only the methylating sense is physiological and ModelSEED's reverse direction would be an SAH-dependent demethylation that this enzyme does not do.

enzyme_name: no dedicated enzyme - decomposition of the extradiol ring-fission product; the ether cleavage happens during 2,3-dihydroxybiphenyl 1,2-dioxygenase (BphC) turnover
organism_context: Pseudomonas cepacia Et4, Cupriavidus sp. WS and related diphenyl-ether degraders
rationale: Pfeifer et al. showed that meta-cleavage of 2,3-dihydroxydiphenyl ether by 2,3-dihydroxybiphenyl 1,2-dioxygenase yields phenol plus 2-pyrone-6-carboxylate 'without participation of free intermediates', so this entry is a formal sub-step of one dioxygenase reaction rather than a reaction with its own catalyst.
direction_note: Lactonisation with expulsion of the 4-bromophenolate is irreversible; re-forming the ring-fission dienoate from 4-bromophenol + 2-pyrone-6-carboxylate does not occur, so ModelSEED's reverse direction is untenable.

enzyme_name: apicidin-F-cluster polyketide/fatty-acid synthase (no single enzyme for the lumped entry)
organism_context: Fusarium fujikuroi apicidin F (APF) cluster
rationale: Three rounds of iterative chain extension plus the required reductions are collapsed into one entry; it corresponds to a multidomain polyketide/fatty-acid synthase operating over several catalytic cycles, not to a single discrete enzymatic step.
direction_note: Malonyl-CoA-driven decarboxylative condensation is irreversible, so the biosynthetic sense is correct despite the entry being grossly unbalanced (status MI:C:-87/H:-116/N:-28/...).

enzyme_name: none identified - spontaneous hydrolysis of the 5-imino group
organism_context: Streptomyces indolmycin pathway (MetaCyc PWY-7770), where dehydroarginine-derived species are handled
rationale: Hydrolysis of (2S)-2-amino-5-iminopentanoate to L-glutamate 5-semialdehyde + ammonia is an ordinary non-enzymatic imine hydrolysis appearing as a shunt around the indolmycin pathway; no catalysing protein is reported in the reconstitution work.
direction_note: Imine hydrolysis in bulk water runs to the carbonyl plus free ammonia; the condensation direction ModelSEED stores would need non-physiological ammonia, and in any case direction here is set by chemistry, not by an enzyme.

enzyme_name: L-azetidine-2-carboxylate hydrolase (AC hydrolase)
organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. strain A2C; periplasmic HAD-superfamily hydrolase
rationale: Gross et al. showed a HAD-superfamily protein from Pseudomonas sp. A2C catalyses azetidine ring opening to 2-hydroxy-4-aminobutyrate using the conserved Asp12 nucleophile; it is a single-activity hydrolase with no second catalytic function reported.
direction_note: Hydrolytic opening of the strained four-membered ring is irreversible and is the detoxification/assimilation direction; the enzyme does not re-cyclise 2-hydroxy-4-aminobutyrate, so ModelSEED's reverse direction is wrong.

enzyme_name: LarE, ATP-dependent sacrificial sulfur insertase (sulfurtransferase) of nickel-pincer cofactor biosynthesis
organism_context: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (sacrificial-cysteine LarE); [4Fe-4S]-dependent LarE in Thermotoga maritima
rationale: LarE carries one overall catalytic activity - ATP-dependent sulfur insertion into the P2CMN carboxylates - and the adenylylation shown here is the first half-step of that single reaction performed in the same active site, not a separate second activity.
direction_note: ATP-dependent carboxylate adenylylation with PPi release is pulled forward and is immediately consumed by the sulfur-transfer step, so the forward sense is the physiological one.

enzyme_name: beta-ODAP synthase (LsBOS), a BAHD acyltransferase
organism_context: Lathyrus sativus (grass pea); works in a two-protein metabolon with the acyl-activating enzyme LsAAE3
rationale: LsBOS is a single-activity BAHD acyltransferase that transfers oxalyl from oxalyl-CoA onto the beta-amino group of L-2,3-diaminopropanoate; the oxalyl-CoA-forming partner LsAAE3 is a separate polypeptide, i.e. a complex rather than a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: The product beta-ODAP is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-5/H:-6/N:-2/O:-5); acyl transfer from a CoA thioester to an amine is irreversible, so the biosynthetic left-to-right sense is correct.

enzyme_name: methanol:coenzyme M methyltransferase system (MtaB methanol:corrinoid methyltransferase + MtaC corrinoid protein + MtaA corrinoid:CoM methyltransferase)
organism_context: Methanosarcina barkeri and M. acetivorans, methylotrophic methanogenesis
rationale: The overall methanol-to-methyl-CoM conversion is carried out by three separate polypeptides (MtaB, MtaC, MtaA) acting as a multi-protein system, which by the multi-subunit exclusion is not bifunctional; each subunit carries one activity and MtaB is the one acting on methanol.
direction_note: The MetaCyc identifier (MTAMBARKMULTI-RXN) is explicitly the multi-enzyme sum, and the product methyl-CoM has been dropped entirely (status MI:C:-3/H:-7/O:-3/S:-2); physiologically the system consumes methanol and CoM, so the forward sense is right even though the reverse has been demonstrated in vitro.

enzyme_name: cichoriin transglucosylase (GH1-type coumarin-glucoside transglucosylase; protein not identified)
organism_context: plants (MetaCyc PWY-7058, esculetin modification; PWY-7186 scopolin/esculin biosynthesis)
rationale: No characterised protein for this transglucosylation could be retrieved in the literature tools; the entry is a MetaCyc half-reaction of a transglucosylase that moves glucose from cichoriin (esculetin 7-O-glucoside) onto the 6-OH of esculetin to give esculin, so its functionality cannot be judged.
direction_note: The donor cichoriin is abstracted to free D-glucose + H2O; the entry is explicitly tagged '(6-O-glucosyltransferase activity)', i.e. the glucose-ADDING half that yields esculin, which is ModelSEED's direction, whereas the LLM's hydrolytic sense is the opposite of what the pathway does.

enzyme_name: 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate deaminase (ACC deaminase, AcdS)
organism_context: Pseudomonas spp., Hansenula saturnus; fold-type II PLP-dependent enzyme
rationale: ACC deaminase is a single-activity PLP enzyme; this entry is the cyclopropane ring-opening half of its mechanism, giving the 2-aminobut-2-enoate (vinylglycine-like) intermediate that then hydrolyses to 2-oxobutanoate + NH3.
direction_note: Relief of cyclopropane ring strain makes the ring opening irreversible; the enzyme never re-forms ACC from 2-aminobut-2-enoate, so ModelSEED's reverse direction is not supported.
